advisory.finding: The keyword-only argument forwarding branch of the facade predicate (matching call.keywords against fn.args.kwonlyargs with `k.value.id == k.arg`), which the docstring presents as the canonical accepted shape `def name(self, a, b, *, c): return self.transport.name(a, b, c=c)`, is never exercised by an ACCEPTED fixture. Both real facades (add_comment, set_relationship) and _FACADE_ACCEPTED use only positional args, so a regression that broke keyword-only forwarding acceptance would not be caught.
merged_from: The facade predicate advertises and implements dedicated handling for keyword-only arguments (`def name(self, a, b, *, c): return self.transport.name(a, b, c=c)`, and the `spec.kwonlyargs`/`call.keywords` block), but no fixture in `_FACADE_ACCEPTED`/`_FACADE_REJECTED` and neither real backend facade (`add_comment(self, r, b)`, `set_relationship(self, from_id, to_id, link_type='Blocks')`) contains a keyword-only argument. The keyword-only forwarding branch is therefore untested: a regression that loosened the keyword equality check (e.g. accepting `c=c.upper()` or a reordered/renamed keyword-only forward) would not be caught by any assertion.
